lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.content: Array<T> is fixed-size, mutable-content, with primitive-optimized variants (IntArray, etc.) avoiding boxing. Real scenario: rarely used over Lists, but common when interoperating with Java or numeric code.

lessons.title: List (Read-Only)
lessons.content: List<T> is a read-only, ordered collection interface. Real scenario: a repository exposing Flow<List<Lesson>> as read-only so the UI can't accidentally mutate cached data.

lessons.title: MutableList
lessons.content: MutableList<T> extends List with add/remove/set operations. Real scenario: building up a list of validation errors as you check each form field.

codeSnippets.code:
val errors = mutableListOf<String>()
if (name.isBlank()) errors.add("Name is required")

lessons.title: Set (Read-Only)
lessons.content: A Set holds unique elements with no defined order guarantee. Real scenario: tracking completed lesson IDs, where a Set naturally prevents duplicate entries.

lessons.title: MutableSet
lessons.content: MutableSet adds add/remove operations to Set. Real scenario: a tag-selection UI toggling tags on/off without ever creating duplicates.

lessons.title: Map (Read-Only)
lessons.content: A Map holds key-value pairs with unique keys, much faster lookup than searching a List. Real scenario: caching lessons by ID for instant lookup on navigation.

codeSnippets.code: val lessonById: Map<String, Lesson> = lessons.associateBy { it.id }

lessons.title: MutableMap
lessons.content: MutableMap adds put/remove and indexed assignment to Map. Real scenario: an in-flight request cache keyed by URL, deduplicating identical concurrent network calls.

lessons.title: ArrayList
lessons.content: ArrayList is the concrete resizable-array-backed implementation returned by mutableListOf(). Real scenario: fast random-access list operations for large collections accessed by index.

lessons.title: HashMap
lessons.content: HashMap is the concrete implementation typically backing mutableMapOf(), O(1) average get/put, no order guarantee. Real scenario: a lookup cache where iteration order doesn't matter.

lessons.title: LinkedHashMap
lessons.content: LinkedHashMap preserves insertion order during iteration, unlike plain HashMap. Real scenario: an LRU cache implementation that reorders entries on access.

lessons.title: HashSet
lessons.content: HashSet backs mutableSetOf(), fast O(1) average contains()/add(), no order guarantee. Real scenario: deduplicating a large list of user IDs where order doesn't matter.

lessons.title: LinkedHashSet
lessons.content: Combines Set uniqueness with insertion-order iteration. Real scenario: deduplicating recently-viewed lesson IDs while preserving view order.

lessons.title: Common Collection Operations
lessons.content: Kotlin's stdlib gives dozens of functional operations without external libraries. Real scenario: sorting lessons by order and taking the first 5 for a featured section.

lessons.title: filter, map, reduce
lessons.content: filter keeps matching elements, map transforms each, reduce/fold combines into a single result. Real scenario: computing total price of only in-stock cart items.

lessons.title: groupBy
lessons.content: groupBy partitions a collection into a Map keyed by a selector function. Real scenario: grouping a flat lesson list by categoryId for the home screen's sections.

codeSnippets.code: val byCategory: Map<String, List<Lesson>> = allLessons.groupBy { it.categoryId }

lessons.title: associate / associateBy / associateWith
lessons.content: associate builds a Map from a Pair-returning transform; associateBy keys by a selector; associateWith computes a value per key. Real scenario: associateBy { it.id } for O(1) lookup.

lessons.title: partition
lessons.content: Splits a collection into two lists based on a predicate in one pass. Real scenario: splitting quiz answers into correct/incorrect for a results screen.

lessons.title: zip
lessons.content: Combines two collections element-by-element into Pairs, stopping at the shorter length. Real scenario: pairing question texts with user answers for a review screen.

lessons.title: flatten and flatMap
lessons.content: flatten collapses nested collections; flatMap does map + flatten in one step. Real scenario: flattening categories' nested lesson lists into one flat list for search.

lessons.title: Sequences (Lazy Collections)
lessons.content: A Sequence evaluates lazily, element-by-element, avoiding intermediate list allocation on chained operations. Real scenario: processing a huge dataset through filter().map().first() efficiently.
